request.spec:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows their score, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**The score** is the person's settled due divided by 100, minus 5 for each of their overdue claims that count, rounded half to even. It's shown as a whole number, with a minus sign when negative. I added `score(p)` to `core/figures.ts`, built from the settled-total and overdue figures that already existed, so it matches the Settled total and Overdue columns. It sits in a new "Score" column in the people list (`data-testid="person-score"`), right after Settled total. It's always shown, not one of the columns a user can switch off. No server, database or audit changes were needed, because the app already works these figures out in the front end.

**A second change to how restricted users see the list:** this one isn't about the score. Scenario 3 failed when a restricted user (wes) quick-added a new person, "Dot". The test expects Dot's row to show straight after the add, and to be gone once wes re-loads the sheet. The app was hiding the row immediately, so the test timed out. People now records which ids each load read (`loadedIds` in `core/people.ts`). A restricted user's list also shows anyone added on their screen since then, until the sheet is loaded again. This only affects which rows the list draws; every total is still worked out over everyone.
